declarations.name: Causal.Causality.PastBoundaryChartData
declarations.statement: structure (C : Causality M) (W Ũ : Opens M) (p : M) : Type u with fields (i) mem : p ∈ Ũ, not_mem : p ∉ W; (ii) inside : Opens M, inside_le : inside ≤ W ⊓ Ũ; (iii) futureClosed : ∀ x ∈ inside, C.Iplus Ũ {x} ⊆ C.Iplus inside {x}; (iv) curve : ℝ → M, chronalCurveOn : C.ChronalCurveOn Ũ curve 0 1, curve_zero : curve 0 = p, curve_mem : ∀ t ∈ Ioc 0 1, curve t ∈ inside; (v) s₀ : ℝ, s₀_mem : s₀ ∈ Ioo 0 1, isCompact_closure : IsCompact (closure (C.Iplus Ũ {p} ∩ C.Iminus Ũ {curve s₀})), closure_subset : closure (C.Iplus Ũ {p} ∩ C.Iminus Ũ {curve s₀}) ⊆ Ũ; (vi) avoid : ∀ K, IsCompact K → K ⊆ Ũ → ∃ σ, C.ChronalCurveOn Ũ σ 0 1 ∧ σ 0 ∉ W ∧ (∀ t ∈ Ioc 0 1, σ t ∈ inside ∧ σ t ∉ K) ∧ C.lt Ũ (curve 1) (σ 1)
declarations.standing: Deliverable (i). Exactly the six fields of the target's evidence, none changed. It is a structure in Type, not Prop: a Prop-valued structure cannot carry the data V, γ̃, s₀ (Lean: 'failed to generate projection … field must be a proof', checked on a scratch file). (vi) quantifies over every compact K ⊆ Ũ, as designed (not weakened).

declarations.name: Causal.Causality.PastBoundaryChart
declarations.statement: C.PastBoundaryChart W Ũ p : Prop := Nonempty (C.PastBoundaryChartData W Ũ p)
declarations.standing: The predicate of the target, Prop-valued, so that the conclusion is ¬ C.PastBoundaryChart W Ũ p.

declarations.name: Causal.Causality.FutureBoundaryChart
declarations.statement: C.FutureBoundaryChart W Ũ p : Prop := C.dual.PastBoundaryChart W Ũ p
declarations.standing: Deliverable (i), the time reversal: Sbierski's future boundary chart, Prop 2.1 as printed. Read for C its field (iii) is I⁻(x, Ũ) ⊆ I⁻(x, V), (2.4) as printed.

declarations.name: Causal.Causality.ChronalCurveOn.pastInextensible_Ioc_of_start_notMem
declarations.statement: [T2Space M] → C.ChronalCurveOn Ũ c 0 1 → s ∈ Ioc 0 1 → (∀ t ∈ Ioc 0 s, c t ∈ W) → c 0 ∉ W → C.PastInextensible W (Ioc 0 s) c ∧ ∀ a ∈ Ioc 0 s, ∀ b ∈ Ioc 0 s, C.ChronalCurveOn W c a b
declarations.standing: Step (a) and the first half of step (d). It is ChronalCurveOn.futureInextensible_of_leaving (SchwCausalLemmas.lean:259) for C.dual and t ↦ c (-t), with U = W ⊔ Ũ, read back by dual_futureInextensible_Ico_iff (:266). Stated for any s ∈ (0, 1], so that (A) can be applied to the initial piece (0, s₀/2].

declarations.name: Causal.Causality.PastBoundaryChartData.Iplus_inter_Iminus_subset
declarations.statement: (d : C.PastBoundaryChartData W Ũ p) → C.CausallyArcConnectedOn W → C.FutureOneConnectedOn W → s ∈ Ioo 0 d.s₀ → C.Iplus W {d.curve s} ∩ C.Iminus W {d.curve d.s₀} ⊆ C.Iplus Ũ {p} ∩ C.Iminus Ũ {d.curve d.s₀}
declarations.standing: Step (b), (4.2)'s ⊆ (sbierski2023c.txt:1108–1109). The curve is γ̃ on [s, s₀], restricted into V, lifted to W, affinely reparametrised over [0, 1] (CurveOn.comp_affine). The closure hypothesis comes from (v) through I⁺(γ̃ s, Ũ) ⊆ I⁺(p, Ũ). The confinement is Iplus_inter_Iminus_subset_of_futureOneConnectedOn (DiamondConfinement.lean:332).

declarations.name: Causal.Causality.PastBoundaryChartData.biUnion_Iplus_inter_Iminus_eq
declarations.statement: (d) → C.CausallyArcConnectedOn W → C.FutureOneConnectedOn W → ⋃ s ∈ Ioo 0 d.s₀, C.Iplus W {d.curve s} ∩ C.Iminus W {d.curve d.s₀} = C.Iplus Ũ {p} ∩ C.Iminus Ũ {d.curve d.s₀}
declarations.standing: (4.2) as an equality (:1077–1109), the option the evidence left to the closer. ⊇ uses I⁺(p, Ũ) = ⋃_{s ∈ (0, s₀/2]} I⁺(γ̃ s, Ũ) (Iplus_eq_biUnion_Ioc, SchwCausalLemmas.lean:167) and field (iii) twice. It needs no (2.2) beyond V ≤ W.

declarations.name: Causal.Causality.PastBoundaryChartData.Iminus_eq_diamond
declarations.statement: [T2Space M] → (d) → C.CausallyArcConnectedOn W → C.FutureOneConnectedOn W → (A): ∀ I γ, C.PastInextensible W I γ → (∀ a ∈ I, ∀ b ∈ I, C.ChronalCurveOn W γ a b) → ⋃ t ∈ I, C.Iplus W {γ t} = W → C.Iminus W {d.curve d.s₀} = C.Iplus Ũ {p} ∩ C.Iminus Ũ {d.curve d.s₀}
declarations.standing: (4.2) combined with Prop 3.6's first claim. Under (A), I⁻(γ̃ s₀, W) is exactly the chart diamond. (A) is applied to γ̃ over (0, s₀/2], so every point of W lies in some I⁺(γ̃ s, W) with s < s₀.

declarations.name: Causal.Causality.PastBoundaryChartData.subset_diamond
declarations.statement: [T2Space M] → (d) → C.CausallyArcConnectedOn W → C.FutureOneConnectedOn W → (A) → S ⊆ C.Iminus W {d.curve d.s₀} → S ⊆ C.Iplus Ũ {p} ∩ C.Iminus Ũ {d.curve d.s₀}
declarations.standing: Deliverable (iii), (4.3) (:1110–1114), for any set inside I⁻(γ̃ s₀, W). It uses neither (B) nor the Cauchy property. This is weaker in hypotheses than the evidence's form ('a Cauchy surface … under (A), (B)'), so that form is a special case.

declarations.name: Causal.Causality.not_pastBoundaryChart_of_flrwType
declarations.statement: [T2Space M] [SecondCountableTopology M] → C.CausallyArcConnectedOn W → C.FutureOneConnectedOn W → (hcaus : ∀ ⦃x y⦄, C.le W x y → C.le W y x → x = y) → (A): ∀ I γ, C.PastInextensible W I γ → (∀ a ∈ I, ∀ b ∈ I, C.ChronalCurveOn W γ a b) → ⋃ t ∈ I, C.Iplus W {γ t} = W → (B): ∀ x ∈ W, ∃ S, C.IsCauchySurfaceOn W S ∧ S ⊆ C.Iminus W {x} → ∀ (Ũ : Opens M) (p : M), ¬ C.PastBoundaryChart W Ũ p
declarations.standing: Deliverable (ii), the main theorem, under the proposed name, with exactly the target's hypotheses. Steps: (B) at γ̃ s₀ gives S; (4.3) puts S in K = closure of the chart diamond; (vi) at K gives σ, past-inextensible in W over (0, 1] by step (a); S ≠ ∅, because W has an inextensible curve (exists_inextensible_of_t1_secondCountable applied to σ); σ 1 ∈ I⁺(S, W) by γ̃ s₀ ≪_Ũ γ̃ 1 ≪_Ũ σ 1 and (iii) at γ̃ s₀; PastInextensible.exists_mem_of_mem_Iplus (PastInextensibleMeetsCauchy.lean:496) gives σ t ∈ S ⊆ K, against (vi).

declarations.name: Causal.Causality.not_futureBoundaryChart_of_flrwType
declarations.statement: [T2Space M] [SecondCountableTopology M] → CausallyArcConnectedOn W → FutureOneConnectedOn W → hcaus → (∀ I γ, C.FutureInextensible W I γ → (∀ a ∈ I, ∀ b ∈ I, C.ChronalCurveOn W γ a b) → ⋃ t ∈ I, C.Iminus W {γ t} = W) → (∀ x ∈ W, ∃ S, C.IsCauchySurfaceOn W S ∧ S ⊆ C.Iplus W {x}) → ∀ Ũ p, ¬ C.FutureBoundaryChart W Ũ p
declarations.standing: Deliverable (ii), the future form. It is the theorem for C.dual. The dual hypotheses are read back through dual_causallyArcConnectedOn, dual_futureOneConnectedOn (the notion is two-sided), dual_pastInextensible_iff, CurveOn.neg and dual_isCauchySurfaceOn.

declarations.name: Causal.IsEMorphismOn.pastInextensible_invComp
declarations.statement: IsEMorphismOn C D W φ → InjOn φ W → LeftInvOn g φ W → V ≤ W → (U : Set N) = φ '' V → D.PastInextensible U I e → C.PastInextensible V I (g ∘ e)
declarations.standing: New general lemma: the one-sided half of the library's inextensible_iff_invComp (CauchyExtension.lean:302), with the same proof plus the final-segment condition. The library had no one-sided transport.

findings: No paper label is involved: 2312.07443 is not ledgered. These findings concern the target's design, Sbierski's text and the library.

The six fields hold as designed; none had to change. The one change of form is that PastBoundaryChart is `Nonempty` of a Type-valued structure PastBoundaryChartData, because a Prop-valued structure cannot carry the data fields V, γ̃, s₀. Lean refuses: 'failed to generate projection … field must be a proof'.
Field (i)'s p ∈ Ũ is redundant: it follows from (iv), since γ̃ is a chronal curve of Ũ with γ̃ 0 = p. It is kept for fidelity to Prop 2.1 i).

The proof uses field (vi) at a single compact set, K = closure (I⁺(p, Ũ) ∩ I⁻(γ̃ s₀, Ũ)) of field (v). It uses (v)'s compactness only to feed (vi). Both could therefore be weakened, to (vi) at that K and to (v) without the compactness, with no change to the proof (the evidence's allowance). The definition keeps 'every compact K ⊆ Ũ', as designed; this is for the author's OQ.

(4.2) holds as an equality from field (iii) alone (biUnion_Iplus_inter_Iminus_eq). Its ⊇ needs (2.2) only as V ≤ W, and Sbierski's (2.2) with (2.4) (sbierski2023c.txt:1107–1108) is exactly what (iii) packages. Under (A), I⁻(γ̃ s₀, W) equals the chart diamond (Iminus_eq_diamond), which is stronger than (4.3).

(4.3) needs neither (B) nor the Cauchy property of the slice: every subset of I⁻(γ̃ s₀, W) lies in the chart diamond once (A), arc-connectedness and future one-connectedness hold. (B) is used once, at the single point γ̃ s₀.

Sbierski does not mention that the slice is non-empty (:1139–1144). In ETT it follows because W has an inextensible causal curve: σ extends to one by exists_inextensible_of_t1_secondCountable (CurvesExtendSecondCountable.lean:1376), and that curve meets S. This uses second countability and T1.

As the evidence said, two of Sbierski's steps are not needed for the contradiction: (4.2)'s ⊇, and I⁺(p̃, Ũ) = ⋃ I⁺(γ̃(s), Ũ) (:1089–1100). Here they are proved anyway, for the equality form of (4.2).

Dimension. On the timelike line no open set has a past boundary chart at any point (timelikeLine_not_pastBoundaryChart), because field (vi) needs room to avoid K. Sbierski's chart likewise needs d ≥ 1 for x₀ ∈ (−ε₁, ε₁)^d (:1137). So the timelike-line witnesses show that the theorem's hypotheses are jointly satisfiable, not that the predicate is inhabited. Sbierski's own d ≥ 2 (Thm 1.5, :151) enters the abstract theorem only through future one-connectedness (Prop 3.1, :477), which is a hypothesis here, as he says at :299.

Library gaps closed in this file: there was no one-sided transport of past-inextensibility along an IsEMorphismOn (now IsEMorphismOn.pastInextensible_invComp), and no proof that an IsSpacetimeExtension is an IsEMorphismOn (now IsSpacetimeExtension.isEMorphismOn). With the second, the CauchyExtension transport lemmas apply to every extension, and isCauchySurfaceOn_image is one of them.
questions: Is Causal.Causality.PastBoundaryChart (six fields; (vi) over every compact K ⊆ Ũ) the ETT notion of record for Sbierski's past boundary chart? It is the programme's definition, adopted unchanged; whether it is the notion of record is the author's question, to become an OQ row (like OQ-154 for IsSpacetimeExtension). Alternatives the proof allows: (vi) only at the closure of the (v) diamond; (v) without compactness once (vi) is so weakened; dropping (i)'s p ∈ Ũ, which (iv) implies.

(A) is read as the evidence states it. It covers every DEC-13 past-inextensible curve of W over any interval that is chronal on its segments, with the union taken over the whole curve. Sbierski's Prop 3.6 (:704–713, :729) concerns future-directed timelike curves parametrised by t over (0, 1), with the union over 0 < s < s₀. The two readings agree, because the theorem applies (A) to the initial piece (0, s₀/2], which is itself past-inextensible (step (a)). That an FLRW spacetime satisfies (A) in the DEC-13 sense is layer 3.
(B) is read at every point of W, as the evidence states it, where Sbierski has it at each γ(s₀) (:715). The slice {t₀} × S^d is read as a DEC-14 Cauchy surface of W. Only γ̃ s₀ is used.

Field (v) is read on ≪: closure (I⁺(p, Ũ) ∩ I⁻(γ̃ s₀, Ũ)) is compact in Ũ, where Sbierski asks compactness of the J_{g̃_w}-diamond (:1077). The I-diamond is contained in it. This is the evidence's reading, recorded here.
The extension corollary rests on OQ-154 (IsSpacetimeExtension as the ETT reading of a C⁰-extension, OPEN). This file records that dependence and decides nothing.

Timelike curves are read as chronal curves (DEC-6) over [0, 1], past inextendible as DEC-13's PastInextensible, and Cauchy hypersurfaces as DEC-14's IsCauchySurfaceOn. These are the library's standing readings, recorded so that no reading is made silently.
kb_proposals: Sbierski's past boundary chart in ETT is Causal.Causality.PastBoundaryChart C W Ũ p. It is Nonempty of the six-field structure PastBoundaryChartData, which lives in Type because a Prop structure cannot hold V, γ̃, s₀. The future chart is its C.dual. Abstract Thm 1.5 is not_pastBoundaryChart_of_flrwType; the extension form is IsSpacetimeExtension.not_pastBoundaryChart_of_flrwType (T-abs-flrw-type).

Every IsSpacetimeExtension is an IsEMorphismOn CN C ⊤ ι (IsSpacetimeExtension.isEMorphismOn), so CauchyExtension's transport of Cauchy surfaces and inextensibility applies to extensions. IsEMorphismOn.pastInextensible_invComp is the one-sided pull-back (T-abs-flrw-type).

On the timelike line no open set has a past boundary chart (timelikeLine_not_pastBoundaryChart). A witness there shows a theorem's hypotheses consistent but not the chart inhabited; an instance needs dimension ≥ 2, which is layer 3 (T-loc-minkowski-past-boundary-chart). Galileo's curve form cannot supply one either, since its diamonds are slabs with non-compact closure.

(2) An instance of the predicate, which is layer 3: T-loc-minkowski-past-boundary-chart, the half-space t > 0 of Minkowski 1+1 at 0, where the fields can be checked by hand. No ETT-layer causality in the library offers a cheap one: it needs dimension ≥ 2 and compact diamond closures, and Galileo's curve form fails (v). (3) The C⁰ derivation of fields (ii)–(vi) (T-loc-c0-past-boundary-chart), using T-abs-boundary-chart-cauchy for (iii).
